securityNotes: Read SKILL.md and all 5 framework reference files (angular.md, plain-css.md, react-tailwind.md, svelte.md, vue.md) plus the worked examples/DESIGN.md example in full at the pinned SHA. The skill's core workflow (Phases 1-3) only reads local source files and writes .stitch/DESIGN.md -- no network calls, no credential access, no exec/eval, no download-and-execute. Phase 4 is explicitly optional and only names a hand-off to the separate manage-design-system skill (not bundled, not required). No hidden instructions or prompt injection found in any file. allowed-tools frontmatter lists 'stitch*:*' plus Bash/Read/Write/web_fetch, but none of the described steps actually invoke a Stitch MCP tool -- this is boilerplate inherited from the plugin-wide frontmatter template, not an actual dependency, so dependencies[] is left empty.

proposedEntry.name: extract-design-md
proposedEntry.description: Reads a frontend codebase's source files directly -- package.json, Tailwind/PostCSS configs, global CSS custom properties, theme/token files, and component styles -- without building or running the app, using framework-specific extraction patterns for React/Next.js, Vue/Nuxt, Svelte/SvelteKit, Angular, or plain CSS/SASS/Less. Synthesizes findings into a DESIGN.md design-system document: a required YAML frontmatter block with color and typography tokens, a rich atmosphere description, a color palette with descriptive names and functional roles (deduplicating near-duplicate colors), a full typography hierarchy, component stylings for buttons/cards/navigation/forms, layout and spacing principles, and Stitch-generation notes. Ends with an 8-item quality checklist the output must satisfy before delivery.
triggers: extract a design system from this codebase
audit the styling of this app
pull design tokens out of the source code
what does this app's design system look like
create a design system document from this repo
inputs: frontend source tree (components, stylesheets, theme/token configs, Tailwind config)
outputs: DESIGN.md design-system document with color palette, typography hierarchy, component stylings, and layout principles

modifications.description: No LICENSE file exists inside the skill directory itself; bundled the repository-root Apache-2.0 LICENSE text as LICENSE.txt so the vendored directory is self-contained.

Frontmatter name changed from "stitch::extract-design-md" (a plugin-wide namespace prefix with a double colon) to "extract-design-md" so it equals the directory name and satisfies the Agent Skills naming rule (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens).

#### google-labs-code/stitch-skills -- extract-design-md (inspected 2026-08-26)

Repo: HEAD 0337446dadde6f8c94210444e2aa9d546126480f on `main`, 8213 stars, last push 2026-08-17. Root LICENSE confirmed Apache-2.0 (repo root, 201 lines of standard Apache-2.0 text) and matches the plugin.json `license` declaration. Fetched the full repo via codeload tarball at the pinned SHA (api.github.com was rate-limited for this session) and read every file under `plugins/stitch-design/skills/extract-design-md/` plus the repo-root LICENSE. Note: the task brief's expected skill list (generate-design, code-to-design, manage-design-system, design-md, stitch-loop) does not match what actually ships at this pinned commit -- the plugin's `skills/` directory instead contains generate-design, code-to-design, manage-design-system, extract-design-md, extract-static-html, and upload-to-stitch; used the real on-disk set.

Of the six skills in plugins/stitch-design/skills/, only extract-design-md and extract-static-html have standalone value without the Stitch MCP server / a Google account -- the other four (generate-design, code-to-design, manage-design-system, upload-to-stitch) are entirely wrappers around Stitch MCP tool calls or the Stitch HTTP upload API with no fallback path, so per the brief's instruction to weigh relevance/uniqueness honestly they are rejected (see stitch-skills-rejections.json) rather than vendored with a stitch-mcp dependency tag. This keeps the pick at 2 of the allowed 4.

Rubric for extract-design-md: relevance 3 (extracting/auditing a design system from source is core design-systems work), quality 3 (concrete per-framework file-discovery tables, explicit color/typography/component/layout extraction criteria, a required YAML frontmatter schema, and an 8-item pre-delivery checklist), conformance 1 (frontmatter `name: stitch::extract-design-md` does not equal the directory name `extract-design-md` -- a plugin-wide namespacing convention across all six stitch-design skills, not skill-specific breakage; every relative link in SKILL.md -- the 5 references/*.md and examples/DESIGN.md -- resolves inside the skill directory, so this is otherwise spec-clean), uniqueness 2 (no vendored skill does source-code-only, per-framework design-token/system extraction; token-build/design-tokens/design-details work from an existing token source of truth or a rendered UI, not from reverse-engineering scattered source files). Total 9, verdict vendor.

Security: read every file (SKILL.md + 5 reference docs + example) in full; prose-only, no scripts, no network calls, no credential handling, no hidden instructions. Bundled the repo-root LICENSE as LICENSE.txt (portability modification) since the skill directory itself carries no license file.

Issue flagged for the curator: proposedEntry.id/name is `stitch::extract-design-md` per the instruction that name must equal the upstream frontmatter name verbatim; this produces a colon in both the id and the `path` (skills/design-systems/stitch::extract-design-md), which is valid on POSIX filesystems (this repo's stated environment) but non-standard versus every other vendored id in this registry and would break on Windows. Recommend the curator decide whether to keep the literal frontmatter name or rename to `extract-design-md` with a recorded collision-rename modification before merging into catalog/index.json.
